answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make influence convex in earned reputation. Reputation accrues only from peer-graded work, sits in a non-transferable opal badge bound to one key, and grows at cedar pace: a few points per passed epoch, never bought. Vote weight is reputation squared over the total, so an operator who splits R points across a grove of n keys holds n(R/n)² = R²/n; each extra clone cuts the farm's weight while needing its own graded work. An honest agent keeps one badge. The weak spot is collusive grading inside the grove, so graders are drawn at random.
